newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal falls, soyoil ends slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal falls, soyoil ends slightly lower.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures ended sharply lower on Tuesday, falling through the 50-day moving average as funds sold, traders said.
Soyoil ended slightly lower with commercial buying amid talk China had purchased Argentine soyoil.
"We're under the moving averages and we're seeing a big change of ownership," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co.
"The Commitment of Traders report showed spec ownership on meal was almost 40,000 contracts. We've liquidated (speculative positions) everything but meal. I think that's what we're struggling with."

Cermak and others said commercials were filling the void left by the fund exodus but buying interest was not strong enough to stop the sharp fall. The July soymeal contract traded as low as $276.70 per ton, the lowest since April 29.

Soyoil bucked the floor-wide bearish trend for much of the session but ended with modest losses as soymeal crumbled. Trade sources pointed to active commercial buying amid rumors China was buying Argentine soyoil.
Soymeal ended $4.90 to $2.40 per ton lower with July down $3.10 at $277.10. Soyoil closed 0.10 to 0.03 cent per lb lower with July off 0.03 at 23.29.

On the day, Rosenthal Collins and Refco Inc each sold 300 lots July soymeal, leading the fund selling wave. Prudential Securities and E.D. and F. Man International each sold 200 July and Dean Witter sold 100 July.
In soyoil, Cargill Inc bought 500 lots July and 100 December, ADM bought 400 July and 200 September and Continental Grain bought 200 September and 150 December, pit sources said.
R.J. O'Brien and Prudential Securities each sold 300 July.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 32,000 lots, compared with Friday's actual volume of 32,490. Soyoil volume was pegged at 13,000 lots, against Friday's 13,369.
